record.content_text:
Another way is to see subtraction as the difference between two numbers. For example, if you have 7 sweets and you eat 4 sweets, you have $7-4=3$ left. The number of sweets you have left is the difference between the sweets you had at the start and the sweets you ate. On a number line, the difference between the numbers 7 and 4 is 3 units.

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-05-012.png)

The number 7 lies 3 units to the positive side of the number 4. Therefore, $7-4=+3$. At the same time, the number 4 lies 3 units to the negative side of the number 7. Therefore, $4-7=-3$.

record_links.rationale: This note clarifies that subtraction order matters for integers.

record.evidence_quote: Use a number line to determine the following: $-5-3$ Use a number line to determine the following: $-4-(-6)$
record.prompt_text:
Use a number line to determine the following: $-5-3$

Use a number line to determine the following: $-4-(-6)$
record.answer_text:
Question 1

Step 1: Identify the two integers that must be subtracted.

$$
\require{enclose}-5\, \enclose{circle}[mathcolor="red"]{-}\,3
$$

The numbers are $-5$ and 3.

Step 2: Draw a number line and show the two numbers on the line.

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-05-013.png)

Step 3: Determine the difference between the two numbers.

The difference between $-5$ and 3 is 8 units.

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-05-014.png)

Step 4: Determine whether the number you are subtracting from lies to the positive or the negative side of the number that is being subtracted.

$-5$ lies to the negative side of 3.

Step 5: Use the information from Step 4 to decide whether the answer is positive or negative.

$$
-5-3=-8
$$

Question 2

Step 1: Identify the two integers that must be subtracted.

$$
\require{enclose}-4\, \enclose{circle}[mathcolor="red"]{-}(-6)
$$

The numbers are $-4$ and $-6$.

Step 2: Draw a number line and show the two numbers on the line.

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-05-015.png)

Step 3: Determine the difference between the two numbers.

The difference between $-4$ and $-6$ is 2 units.

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-05-016.png)

Step 4: Determine whether the number you are subtracting from lies to the positive or the negative side of the number that is being subtracted.

$-4$ lies to the positive side of $-6$.

Step 5: Use the information from Step 4 to decide whether the answer is positive or negative.

$$
-4-(-6)=2
$$

record.answer_text:
Identify the two integers that must be subtracted.

$$
\require{enclose}-4\,\enclose{circle}[mathcolor="red"]{-}\,3
$$

The number 3 must be subtracted from the number $-4$.

Method 1: Regard subtraction as another form of addition.

$$
\require{enclose}-4\,\enclose{circle}[mathcolor="red"]{-}\,3=-4\,\enclose{circle}[mathcolor="red"]{+}(-3)
$$

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-05-021.png)

$$
\therefore -4+(-3)=-7
$$

Method 2: Regard subtraction as the difference between two numbers.

$$
\require{enclose}-4\,\enclose{circle}[mathcolor="red"]{-}\,3
$$

![](https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-05-022.png)

$-4$ lies to the negative side of 3.

$$
\therefore -4-3=-7
$$

The two methods give the same answer.

closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.proposed_objective_text: Write subtraction of integers as addition of opposite integers.
closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.evidence_quote: Subtracting a number is the same as adding the "opposite" of the number.
closest_candidate_atomic_objectives.rationale: The textbook teaches and assesses a symbolic rewrite rule for subtraction of integers. That is a distinct objective from solving subtraction on a number line, even though it supports the same broader topic.
